root_cause.text: In `drivers/ufs/core/ufshcd.c`, `__ufshcd_wl_suspend()` canceled `hba->ufs_rtc_update_work` too late—after entering `ufshcd_vops_suspend()`—allowing the RTC delayed work to race with suspend-time clock gating and call UFS MMIO/query paths during hardware quiesce, which can trigger an SError.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&hba->ufs_rtc_update_work);` from after `ufshcd_vops_suspend(hba, pm_op, POST_CHANGE)` to immediately after `flush_work(&hba->eeh_work);` and before `ufshcd_vops_suspend(..., PRE_CHANGE)`, and the CVE text states this race let `ufshcd_rtc_work()` run while `ufshcd_vops_suspend()` was performing clock gating, causing `ufshcd_update_rtc()` to trigger an Asynchronous SError.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending RTC update work during suspend to prevent it from executing across the power transition.
intent_record.what: In __ufshcd_wl_suspend(), a new call to cancel_delayed_work_sync(&hba->ufs_rtc_update_work) was added immediately after flush_work(&hba->eeh_work) and before ufshcd_vops_suspend(..., PRE_CHANGE).
intent_record.how: This ensures any pending RTC update delayed work is synchronously canceled during suspend, preventing it from running concurrently with or after the suspend transition and avoiding unintended RTC update activity while the device is suspending.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the synchronous cancellation of RTC update work from the suspend path.
intent_record.what: The call to `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&hba->ufs_rtc_update_work);` was removed from `__ufshcd_wl_suspend()` just before the function jumps to `out`.
intent_record.how: On successful suspension path, the driver no longer synchronously cancels the RTC update delayed work at this point, allowing that work to remain scheduled or be handled elsewhere instead of being forcibly stopped during suspend completion.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it moves/cancels the RTC update work during suspend to prevent the delayed work from racing with hardware quiesce and accessing UFS MMIO/query paths, which is exactly the vulnerability condition.

The root cause is that RTC update work was canceled too late during suspend, creating a race with clock gating and UFS MMIO access. This change removes the synchronous cancellation from the suspend path, directly modifying the code involved in that race and therefore relating to the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This call occurs before the RTC update work is canceled in the pre-fix flow, which means suspend-time hardware quiesce can overlap with pending RTC delayed work. That ordering is the root cause of the race leading to MMIO/query access during clock gating.

This is the exact cancellation that was removed from the suspend path. In the vulnerable version it was placed too late, after suspend-time operations had already begun, allowing the RTC work to race with hardware quiesce and trigger the SError.

vuln_statements.explanation: This suspend callback is invoked before the RTC delayed work is canceled in the pre-fix flow, so RTC update work can still run while suspend-time clock gating/quiesce is underway. That ordering creates the race that allows UFS MMIO/query access during hardware suspend and can trigger an SError.

This cancellation happens too late in the vulnerable version, after suspend-time operations have already started. Because the delayed RTC work is only synchronized here, it can overlap with hardware quiesce and race into MMIO/query paths during clock gating.

bic_trace_step.reason: This snippet clearly shows the suspend/resume handling for the newly added RTC work, and it contains the vulnerable ordering. In `__ufshcd_wl_suspend()` the code does `ret = ufshcd_vops_suspend(hba, pm_op, POST_CHANGE);` and only afterwards calls `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&hba->ufs_rtc_update_work);`. Per the root cause, canceling the RTC delayed work after entering `ufshcd_vops_suspend()` is too late and allows the work to race with suspend-time quiesce/clock gating. The fix would require canceling the work before the suspend path reaches hardware quiesce; that is not present here. The rest of the diff also confirms RTC work is scheduled periodically (`schedule_delayed_work(&hba->ufs_rtc_update_work, ...)`) and rescheduled on resume, so the vulnerable construct is present.
